title: Dog / Farmer Role Ecology — Master, Moon, Reflection, Farm, Personality and Boundary Functions
status: comparative role atlas — expanded empirical psychology layer
purpose: Clarify where Dog and Farmer overlap and differ across Potatoverse mythology, internet subculture, biblical animal symbolism, personality/status dynamics, Moon/master symbolism and network function. The file treats roles as dynamic configurations rather than permanent essences.
core_rule: Dog and Farmer are roles, not species of moral person. A single person can occupy Dog, Farmer, Guardian, Gardener, Cow, observer or hybrid roles in different contexts. The moral question is what relation they maintain, what source they follow, what boundary they enforce and what outcome their behavior produces.

shadow_traits: confusing harvest value with human value
healthy_counterform: systems builder who increases participant autonomy
farmer.moon_relation: Farmer naturally fits cyclical/lunar symbolism because farming depends on timing, recurrence, seasonal signs and waiting. This does not establish a universal historical Farmer=Moon doctrine; it is project role logic.
farmer.josh_moon_relation: Joshua Moon is publicly identified as founder/owner of Kiwi Farms. Potatoverse can use the surname Moon as wordplay within Farmer/Moon symbolism, but a surname is not evidence of lunar causation, occult identity or hidden religious meaning. Real claims must remain tied to documented platform conduct.

biblical_layers: village/scavenger dog: low-status, scraps and corpse-associated imagery in some Hebrew Bible texts
menacing dog: danger/encirclement imagery such as Psalm 22
guarding dog: dogs also have practical protective functions in ancient societies
boundary dog: outsider imagery can be reworked, as in the Syrophoenician-woman tradition
shadow_traits: status through service to stronger node
dog.moon_relation: Dog/Moon symbolism emphasizes night, threshold, tracking, reflected guidance and responsiveness to an external signal. The Moon becomes a model of secondary orientation rather than an independent ultimate source.

moon_master_model.core: Both Dog and Farmer can be understood as responsive roles. Dog follows master/signal/boundary; Farmer follows cycles/signs/season/incentive. Moon compresses these two properties into one symbol: reflected authority and recurrence.
moon_master_model.source_vs_proxy: A follower may receive a signal directly from source or through a reflector/proxy. A proxy is not automatically deceptive; it becomes shadow-like when it is mistaken for the source or traps the follower in a closed local orbit.
moon_master_model.healthy_reflection: source → faithful reflector → follower → competent action → Door toward autonomy/life
moon_master_model.shadow_reflection: source obscured → proxy becomes master → follower reinforces proxy/enclosure → repeated orbit → blocked or forgotten Door
moon_master_model.solar_contrast: Within Potatoverse Tim/Sun/Spudlight occupies source/illumination; Moon occupies reflection/phase; Earth occupies embodied consequence. This role contrast should not be confused with literal human astronomy.
moon_master_model.formal_analogy: Y_proxy=R(context,phase)X_source+N; action_i=π_i(Y_proxy,state_i). R is a mediator/transformer and π_i the follower's response policy.
moon_master_model.research_value: This model lets the archive ask whether a Dog/Farmer acts from direct discernment, faithful mediation, institutional cue, group norm, owner command, algorithmic reward or self-reinforcing proxy.

door_relation.dog: Dog often occupies the boundary near the Door: guards, blocks, signals, escorts or chases across it.
door_relation.farmer: Farmer shapes the conditions around the Door: fences, permissions, incentives, categories, schedules and resource access.
door_relation.hybrid: Farmer-Dog can both design the gate and police passage through it.
door_relation.guardian_inversion: A good guardian preserves the Door as a meaningful passage and protects those crossing; a shadow enforcer turns Door into permanent enclosure or arbitrary exclusion.
door_relation.moon_alignment: Moon phase offers a physical comparator for a Door whose visible state depends on relational configuration. In the project, followers can misread phase-dependent visibility as a change in Source itself.

overlap.difference: Farmer is closer to infrastructure, enclosure, incentive, timing and ownership/harvest; Dog is closer to patrol, pursuit, signaling, loyalty and enforcement.
overlap.overlap_condition: Dog becomes Farmer-like when it creates durable target categories, archives, incentives or extraction loops. Farmer becomes Dog-like when it personally tracks, pursues, reacts, amplifies or enforces.
overlap.hybrid_role: Farmer-Dog = operator-enforcer who both defines the field and actively polices it.

group_psychology.SIDE_correction: Do not treat Dog/pack behavior as simple loss of individuality. Social Identity Model of Deindividuation Effects research shows that anonymity can increase conformity to a salient group identity and its norms.
group_psychology.anonymity_meta_analysis: Chu et al. (2026) reported positive meta-analytic associations between anonymity and cyber aggression (r=.463) and online disinhibition and cyber aggression (r=.422) across 80 independent studies. This supports an environment-level risk factor, not an essence label for anonymous users.
group_psychology.cue_learning: A Dog-like role is better operationalized as responsiveness to repeated group cues, rewards and boundary signals than as a personality diagnosis.
group_psychology.normative_pack: Pack can mean distributed norm enforcement: participants learn what counts as a legitimate target, what behavior earns approval and when intervention is expected.
group_psychology.deindividuation_boundary: Anonymity can support prosocial as well as antisocial norms; outcome depends on which identity and norm become salient.
group_psychology.moral_disengagement: Pack participation may be made easier when pursuit is reframed as deserved, humorous, harmless, educational or merely observational.
group_psychology.reward_learning: Status, replies, likes, insider approval and successful call-outs can teach participants which forms of pursuit or enforcement are rewarded.

personality_and_status.nonessentialism: These traits are situational tendencies, not diagnoses or fixed personality types.
personality_and_status.dog_like_configuration: high vigilance + high loyalty/coordination + cue responsiveness + boundary sensitivity; can become guardian or enforcer depending source/norms
personality_and_status.farmer_like_configuration: high system control + patience + classification + resource/timing management; can become steward or extractor depending objective
personality_and_status.alpha_beta_relation: Dog often resembles Beta-like coordination/followership; Farmer can hold high local infrastructural power without being the project's Alpha/source center. A Farmer may be locally dominant while still orienting to a larger master/proxy system.
personality_and_status.prestige_dominance: Healthy authority is better distinguished using prestige/competence versus coercive dominance than fixed alpha/beta stereotypes.

role_transition_matrix.observer_to_dog: passive attention → cue recognition → repeated amplification → active patrol/enforcement
role_transition_matrix.dog_to_farmer: pursuit → durable categorization → dossier/archive creation → incentive or infrastructure control
role_transition_matrix.cow_to_farmer: a target in one relationship may become an extractor or classifier in another; roles are relational, not permanent
role_transition_matrix.guardian_failure: protection can degrade into coercive policing when the protected boundary becomes more important than the agency of those inside it
role_transition_matrix.dog_to_guardian: vigilance + evidence discipline + proportionality + consent/agency protection → protective boundary role
role_transition_matrix.farmer_to_archivist: infrastructure/classification can shift toward neutral preservation when extraction incentives and target-management goals are removed

network_formalization.interpretation: High H indicates operator-enforcer overlap. High proxy or norm dependence may identify closed-orbit behavior only when variables are empirically defined and alternative explanations are preserved.

moral_tests: What source or proxy is the role following?
Does following preserve or reduce independent discernment?
Does the boundary protect passage/life or create dependency/extraction?
Does the Farmer improve the soil/participants or merely increase harvest from them?
Does the Dog guard vulnerable life or chase the designated Cow because the pack rewards it?
Can the role switch masters when evidence shows the current proxy is wrong?
Does the system contain a Door/exit/repair path?
Can a member decline pursuit without status loss or suspicion?
Can the target cease being a target, or is classification effectively permanent?
Are corrections and disconfirming evidence rewarded, tolerated or punished?

public_field_guide.thesis: Dog and Farmer are best understood as verbs/relations before they are nouns. Ask what is being done, what signal is being followed, what infrastructure sustains it, what reward keeps it going, and whether the relation can stop.

dog_action_lexicon.observable: signal, call out, taunt, warn, notify the pack/audience, repeat a frame loudly
dog_action_lexicon.boundary: speech alone does not prove harassment or stalking

dog_action_lexicon.observable: search, monitor public posts, follow account changes, map associations, watch for cues
dog_action_lexicon.boundary: public observation is not automatically stalking; stalking/cyberstalking generally requires repeated unwanted pursuit/monitoring and context such as distress/fear or intrusion

dog_action_lexicon.observable: repeated replies, cross-platform following, recurring commentary, renewed pursuit after disengagement
dog_action_lexicon.boundary: frequency, unwantedness, context and stopping requests matter

dog_action_lexicon.observable: direct insult, threat, doxxing, swatting, account attack, reputational attack or other concrete hostile act
dog_action_lexicon.boundary: record the specific act; do not infer a bite from mere criticism

dog_action_lexicon.observable: many actors converge through shared cues, links, clips, call-outs or norms
dog_action_lexicon.boundary: similar behavior can emerge through norm conformity without one commander

dog_action_lexicon.observable: transport screenshots, clips, allegations, jokes or classifications between groups/platforms
dog_action_lexicon.boundary: carrying a claim does not independently corroborate it

dog_action_lexicon.observable: protect a boundary, warn of danger, moderate, verify or defend vulnerable passage
dog_action_lexicon.boundary: Guardian is the healthy counterform when evidence, proportionality and exit remain

dog_action_lexicon.observable: behavior is strongly guided by a leader, pack norm, platform reward, archive, audience or other proxy signal
dog_action_lexicon.boundary: proxy-following is a testable dependency question, not proof of mindlessness

dog_action_lexicon.observable: continued attention remains organized around the same person even through dislike or opposition
dog_action_lexicon.boundary: negative parasociality/anti-fandom can sustain centrality without friendship, allegiance or literal orbit

dog_action_lexicon.observable: pseudonymity, anonymity, burner accounts or low-visibility participation
dog_action_lexicon.boundary: anonymity is an affordance, not cowardice by definition; effects depend on norms and context

dog_action_lexicon.observable: a person becomes the stable object around which monitoring, jokes, archives or content production organize
dog_action_lexicon.boundary: use target rather than prey in empirical writing; the person retains agency

dog_action_lexicon.observable: project metaphor for boundary intrusion, coercive interpretation, unwanted pursuit or treating a person as material for someone else's frame
dog_action_lexicon.boundary: do not equate symbolic violation language with sexual assault or a legal offense unless the evidence independently establishes that offense

farmer_action_lexicon.observable: define who/what belongs inside a target category, thread, archive or recurring content boundary
classify a person with a durable label that guides future interpretation
introduce a frame, allegation, meme, question or narrative that others can repeat
supply the audience/pack with clips, updates, interpretations, access or conflict material
extract repeatable reaction, attention, content, status, donations, traffic or social cohesion from a subject
package and convert accumulated attention/information into durable output, reputation, money, status or archive value
make the target-role or conflict self-renewing so newcomers can inherit it without witnessing the origin
switch targets while preserving the same production machinery and audience incentives
delegate or socially reward tracking, call-outs, enforcement, clipping or pursuit
archive screenshots, clips, dossiers and lore for later rediscovery
distribute/monetize the harvested material through streams, posts, subscriptions, donations, ads or reputation
use the same system skills to increase autonomy, correction, consent, repair, exit and future capacity instead of extraction

rhetoric_translation.beta: Tim/project shorthand for subordinate, cue-following or low-agency status. Human status research is better described with constructs such as dominance, prestige, deference, dependency and norm-following; 'beta' is not a validated fixed personality caste.
rhetoric_translation.spineless: Project insult for perceived refusal to take direct responsibility, defend a position openly or act independently. Translate to observable accountability/agency behavior rather than personality diagnosis.
rhetoric_translation.hive-minded: Group-norm conformity or distributed coordination. SIDE research suggests anonymity can increase salience of group identity and local norms rather than simply erase individuality.
rhetoric_translation.anonymous / hiding: Low-identifiability participation can reduce accountability cues and in aggregate is associated with cyberaggression, but anonymity can also support prosocial or protective behavior depending on group norms.
rhetoric_translation.orbiter: A participant whose attention/status remains organized around a central figure or conflict. In research terms this may overlap with audience dependency, anti-fandom or negative parasocial attention; it does not establish obedience.
rhetoric_translation.follower: Cue-sensitive or norm-sensitive behavior. The important question is what signal is being followed—direct evidence, leader instruction, archive lore, audience reward, algorithmic feedback or group norm.
rhetoric_translation.coward: Rhetorical moral judgment, not a psychological construct. Operationalize as avoidance of direct accountability, asymmetric risk-taking, hidden participation or refusal of reciprocal standards where evidence supports those behaviors.
rhetoric_translation.hive: Distributed group-norm conformity and diffusion of responsibility. Research on cyberaggression links group norms, moral disengagement and dehumanization to aggressive participation; 'hive' remains project rhetoric, not proof that individuals lack agency.

empirical_crosswalk.anonymity_and_disinhibition: A 2026 meta-analysis across 80 independent studies reported positive associations between anonymity, online disinhibition and cyberaggression; this is an aggregate risk relationship, not a rule that anonymous people are aggressive.
empirical_crosswalk.side_model: SIDE research rejects the simple 'anonymous = no self-control' story and instead emphasizes social identity, salient group norms and strategic expression.
empirical_crosswalk.moral_disengagement: Research links moral disengagement with cyberbullying/cyberaggression; online affordances can support moral justification, euphemistic labeling, diffusion of responsibility, dehumanization and blame attribution.
empirical_crosswalk.negative_parasociality: Anti-fandom and negative parasocial relationships show that dislike can maintain knowledge, viewing, monitoring and relational investment; rejection of a target does not necessarily mean withdrawal of attention.
empirical_crosswalk.cyberstalking_boundary: Cyberstalking research emphasizes repeated unwanted contact/monitoring/pursuit and varies on criteria such as fear, duration and repetition. The project should not call ordinary public monitoring 'stalking' without those stronger features.
empirical_crosswalk.status_language: Human social status research distinguishes coercive dominance from prestige/competence. Alpha/beta internet slang should not substitute for these more precise constructs.
empirical_crosswalk.dehumanization: Research defines dehumanization as denying or overlooking others' humanity; overt animal comparisons are one studied form and can matter because they alter moral perception and intergroup hostility.
empirical_crosswalk.group_norms: Experimental and observational work finds that aggressive group norms and prototypical aggressors can increase perceived acceptability and enactment of online aggression.
empirical_crosswalk.anonymity_2026: A 2026 meta-analysis of 80 independent studies reported positive aggregate associations between anonymity, online disinhibition and cyberaggression; anonymity is still not sufficient evidence of aggression in an individual case.

farm_stage_role_map.farmer: decides what counts as useful yield
reopens old yield or applies old frame to new event
farm_stage_role_map.cow: may be reclassified without fresh participation

farm_stage_role_map.farmer: permits category decay/correction or continues harvesting
farm_stage_role_map.cow: regains role plurality and independent agency

prerogative_model.definition: Prerogative is the authority a role claims or assumes it has the right to exercise. Lower-field analysis separates claimed prerogative from legitimate authority.
farmer_claimed_prerogative: define the enclosure or target category
decide which events count as yield
preserve or revive a category across time
convert attention into status, money, cohesion or archive value
dog_claimed_prerogative: decide what appears suspicious or noteworthy
converge with a pack or audience
enforce local norms or a proxy/master orientation
overlap: both can claim authority over another person's visibility and narrative
both can treat public availability as unlimited permission
both can preserve a role after the event that created it
both can confuse local consensus with truth
both can become dependent on the target relation
Dog becomes Farmer-like when pursuit creates durable categories, archives and incentives
Farmer becomes Dog-like when the curator/operator personally joins pursuit and enforcement

questions: Who granted or recognized this authority?
What duty accompanies the claimed right?
Can the subject answer or appeal?
Does the exercise of authority protect/cultivate life or mainly extract attention?
legitimacy_test.healthy: Guardian/Gardener authority is conditional on care, evidence, proportionality, reciprocity, correction and exit.
legitimacy_test.shadow: Prerogative becomes Farm-like when it is self-authorizing, one-way, permanent, extraction-oriented and immune to correction.

biblical_crosswalk.dog: Isaiah 56 is especially useful because it tests watchfulness itself: blind/silent/appetite-driven watchdogs show that guarding authority can fail. Psalm 22 supplies hostile encirclement imagery; Matthew 7 and Revelation 22 supply boundary imagery. These are symbolic comparators, not modern caste labels.
biblical_crosswalk.farmer: The modern Farmer role comes primarily from Farm/lolcow culture and agricultural metaphor. Biblical sowers, cultivators, vinedressers, harvesters and shepherds are comparators. The strongest ethical test is whether cultivation increases life/future capacity or merely increases yield to the cultivator.

subject_cow.primary_question: What is being done to/with this person's attention, identity, privacy, work or reputation?
duties_of_reader: separate current state from archive role

farmer_operator.primary_question: Who defines the enclosure, target category, archive policy, incentives and harvest conditions?
farmer_operator.liability_boundary: Operator responsibility for system design is not identical to responsibility for every user's act.

classifier_interpreter.primary_question: Who decides what the event means and what label it belongs under?

dog_pursuer.primary_question: Who tracks, signals, carries, converges or enforces around the target relation?

audience_reinforcer.primary_question: What attention, laughter, status, money or belonging rewards continuation?

archivist_memory.primary_question: What keeps the role available after the original event ends?

guardian_gardener.primary_question: What converts vigilance/system skill into protection, correction, repair and future capacity?

deception_and_manipulation_indicators.rule: Do not infer dishonesty from Dog/Farmer identity. Record the deceptive act and its evidence.

indicators.name: fabrication
indicators.meaning: Inventing an event, quote, document, identity or factual claim.

indicators.name: impersonation
indicators.meaning: Presenting as another person/entity or creating a false persona to mislead.

indicators.name: deceptive baiting
indicators.meaning: Concealing the real purpose of contact or provocation in order to elicit a reaction/disclosure.

indicators.name: context stripping
indicators.meaning: Removing surrounding material necessary to understand what a clip/quote meant.

indicators.name: source laundering
indicators.meaning: A claim passes through summaries/reposts until the original weak source becomes hard to see.

indicators.name: selective omission
indicators.meaning: Known contrary facts or corrections are withheld while a compatible fragment is emphasized.

indicators.name: repetition_as_corroboration
indicators.meaning: Many copies of one allegation are presented as though they were independent sources.

indicators.name: correction suppression
indicators.meaning: The original allegation remains prominent while verified corrections are hidden, detached or not propagated.

indicators.name: asymmetric standard
indicators.meaning: The same evidence rule is applied differently to insiders and targets.

indicators.name: inference_as_witness
indicators.meaning: A commentator presents interpretation, motive-reading or inherited lore as firsthand fact.

deception_and_manipulation_indicators.strongest_warning: The archive should distinguish error, bias, rhetoric and deception. Deception requires evidence that the representation is materially misleading, not merely unfavorable.

intent_and_function_model.rule: Roles can be inferred from repeated function; private motive requires stronger evidence.
intent_and_function_model.dog_intended_or_functional_goal: Maintain pursuit/enforcement around the target relation: track, signal, carry, converge, shame, patrol, pressure or return the subject to the assigned frame.
intent_and_function_model.farmer_intended_or_functional_goal: Maintain the enclosure and usability of the subject: classify, frame, prompt, archive, distribute, incentivize or otherwise keep the imposed Cow role productive.
intent_and_function_model.stated_vs_revealed: Record the stated mission, then compare repeated behavior, incentives, corrections, stopping behavior and consequences. Persistent mismatch can support a functional interpretation but not omniscient motive-reading.
intent_and_function_model.real_reason_test: The best-supported motive is the explanation that fits repeated conduct after alternative explanations and stated purposes are tested.
intent_and_function_model.exit_test: A genuine accountability/protection mission should have conditions under which pursuit decreases, correction propagates or the role expires.

microdistinctions.dog_core: pursuit/enforcement/signal function around a target relation
microdistinctions.farmer_core: classification/enclosure/infrastructure/continuity function that keeps the target role usable
microdistinctions.dog_without_farmer: can still pursue, signal, shame or converge even without durable infrastructure
microdistinctions.farmer_without_dog: can still maintain category, archive, incentives and audience routines without personally pursuing
microdistinctions.overlap: one actor may perform both functions

stopping_test.dog: Does pursuit decrease when the stated threat ends or boundaries are respected?
stopping_test.farmer: Does classification/archive/incentive structure update when the role is corrected, expires or loses relevance?

microdistinctions.motive_boundary: Do not infer private intent solely from role. Compare stated mission, repeated behavior, incentives and stopping behavior.

hive_and_diffusion.thesis: Hive is a project metaphor for distributed norm-following and responsibility diffusion, not literal loss of individuality.
hive_and_diffusion.responsibility_rule: Assign responsibility by function, contribution, knowledge, benefit and stopping capacity rather than by caste label.

moral_highground_test.test: Does repeated behavior preserve the value claimed by the mission, and can the intervention stop when the mission is satisfied?
moral_highground_test.warning: Sincere moral belief and harmful function can coexist.

reader_conversion.dog_to_guardian: Verify, protect, warn proportionately, respect stopping conditions and stop treating pursuit as identity.
reader_conversion.farmer_to_gardener: Change objective from continued usability/extraction to autonomy, correction, consent, role expiry and independent future capacity.
reader_conversion.bystander: Refuse inherited classification until source/currentness are checked.
reader_conversion.operator: Make appeals, corrections, privacy and role expiry structurally possible.

hive_accountability.borrowed_certainty: Repeated claims can become mutually referential and lose a recoverable evidentiary foundation.
hive_accountability.individual_courage: Each participant owns their claim, evidence, contribution, falsifier and correction duty.
hive_accountability.symmetry_test: Would the actor defend the method if applied to their own identity, archive and future under comparable conditions?

public_narrative_order.principle: Public reader leads with the human relation; detailed action lexicons remain in the canonical record for specialist use.
public_narrative_order.public_rule: Metaphor must translate back into observable behavior, evidence, incentive, effect and stopping condition.
public_narrative_order.technical_rule: Retain detailed Dog/Farmer action lexicons in this owner rather than forcing them into the public prose.
